target.title: feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening
target.body:
# PR Title

`feat(gateway): pre-handshake WS verifyClient with Sec-Fetch-Site and forwarded-header hardening`

---

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw's gateway already validates browser `Origin` on the WebSocket path, but only **post-handshake** (in `src/gateway/server/ws-connection/connect-admission.ts`, after the socket is already open), and it does **not** defend against:

- **Header-smuggling / contradiction attacks** — a client forging `X-Forwarded-For` to disagree with `Forwarded` (or vice-versa) to confuse the resolved client IP / trust decision.
- **Cross-site WebSocket initiations (CSRF / DNS-rebinding class)** — there is no `Sec-Fetch-Site` gate anywhere in `main` (`git grep` confirms zero `sec-fetch-site` enforcement in `src/`).
- **Proto contradiction** — `X-Forwarded-Proto` / `Forwarded proto` disagreeing with the actual socket transport (without breaking legitimate TLS-terminating trusted proxies).

These gaps are the WebSocket sibling of the now-closed HTTP ingress CSRF findings **#102834** and **#96486**, and sit *under* the origin-allowlist work in **#98924** (which decides *which* origins pass, not *when/how the gate runs*).

This PR adds a self-contained **pre-handshake** `verifyClient` gate attached to the gateway `WebSocketServer({ noServer: true })`, so unauthenticated or forged clients never complete the HTTP 101 upgrade.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Pre-handshake beats post-handshake.** Running the checks in `verifyClient` (before the 101) means a rejected client never gets a live socket, matching the defense-in-depth posture maintainers expect for a network-exposed gateway.
- **Reuses the shared `checkBrowserOrigin`** rather than reinventing origin logic, so allowlist / same-host / loopback behavior stays consistent with the HTTP/WS admission paths.
- **All strictness is opt-in and default-off** (`gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation`, `rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders`, `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests`), so existing deployments have **zero behavior change**. Non-browser clients (CLI, native apps) send no `Origin` and pass through; they authenticate post-handshake as today.
- **Trusted proxies are correctly exempted** from the proto-mismatch check — a TLS-terminating proxy legitimately presents plaintext to the gateway.

This is complementary to **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`): that PR extends *which* loopback origins are allowed; this PR adds the *enforcement layer* (pre-handshake gate, header contradiction, `Sec-Fetch-Site`). Neither duplicates the other.

## Prior Attempt & What Improved

This is a follow-up to my earlier (closed) PR **#35109** (`fix(gateway): surgical proxy-aware origin validation`), which edited the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` on the *post-handshake* WS path. Compared to that attempt, this PR:

- Moves the gate to **pre-handshake** (`verifyClient` before the 101) instead of extending the post-handshake check — a rejected client never opens a socket.
- Adds the **`Sec-Fetch-Site` cross-site rejection** and **`X-Forwarded-For` vs `Forwarded` IP-contradiction** checks that #35109 did not cover.
- Keeps the change **self-contained** in `verify-client.ts` + `forwarded-headers.ts` rather than widening the shared `checkBrowserOrigin` contract used by every HTTP/WS caller.
- Ran the `autoreview` closeout gate before opening; it caught a real **`Origin: null` bypass** (a literal `null` origin was treated like an absent header and skipped all browser validation). Fixed in `verify-client.ts` with a regression test — the gate now only fast-passes on a *truly absent* Origin.

The goal was to take the earlier direction, make it architecturally cleaner, and actually vet it before asking for review.

## User Impact

- Network-exposed gateways gain a pre-handshake defense against forged forwarded headers and cross-site WebSocket CSRF, with **no config change required** for existing users (all new behavior opt-in).
- Operators who want stricter posture can enable:
  - `gateway.security.strictHeaderValidation` — reject duplicate / comma-chained sensitive proxy headers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectUntrustedProxyHeaders` — reject proxy headers from non-trusted peers.
  - `gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` — reject `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site` / `cross-origin` WebSocket upgrades. **Off by default**; opt in only when every legitimate browser WS client is same-origin to the gateway. Loopback aliases (e.g. `localhost` -> `127.0.0.1`) are legitimately flagged cross-site by browsers, so the gate stays opt-in and `checkBrowserOrigin` remains authoritative.

## Evidence

Real gateway/WS behavior, driven through the actual `verify-client` factory (not mocked):

```
# Trusted proxy presenting plaintext X-Forwarded-Proto -> ACCEPTED (proto-mismatch exempt)
remote=127.0.0.1  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=true

# Identical request from an UNTRUSTED peer -> REJECTED
remote=198.51.100.7  origin=https://app.example.com  x-forwarded-proto=https  -> ok=false

# Cross-site WebSocket initiation from a browser -> REJECTED (Sec-Fetch-Site)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=https://evil.example.com  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Literal "null" browser origin -> REJECTED (no longer skips the gate)
remote=192.0.2.10  origin=null  sec-fetch-site=cross-site -> ok=false

# Non-browser client with no Origin header -> PASSES THROUGH
remote=192.0.2.10  (no Origin)  -> ok=true
```

- Test file: `src/gateway/server/verify-client.test.ts` — **5/5 passing** (trusted-proxy wiring regression, untrusted-peer reject, cross-site reject, `Origin: null` reject, non-browser pass-through). The trusted-proxy case guards a real prior regression where `gateway.trustedProxies` was never read at the call site.
- `tsgo` typecheck: **clean** on both `verify-client.ts` and `forwarded-headers.ts`.
- `autoreview` (Codex, high reasoning): initially reported the `Origin: null` bypass; after the fix, no accepted/actionable findings.

## Scope / Out of scope

- **In scope:** `src/gateway/server/verify-client.ts` (new, wired at `server-runtime-state.ts`), `src/gateway/forwarded-headers.ts` (validators), their tests, and the `gateway.security.*` config surface in `src/config/types.gateway.ts` + `src/config/zod-schema.ts`.
- **Out of scope (left to maintainer decision):** the `#98924` allowlist-wildcard contract, and the broader `gateway.browserOrigins` client/role-scoped policy direction.
- **`Sec-Fetch-Site` note for reviewers:** upstream deliberately avoids a blanket `cross-site` reject on MCP **HTTP** because browsers flag legit local MCP as cross-site. This PR mirrors that posture for the **WebSocket upgrade** path: the reject is **opt-in** (`gateway.security.rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests: true`) and runs *after* `checkBrowserOrigin`, so the existing origin allowlist / loopback-alias admission (shipped in v2026.4.15, PR #66665) remains authoritative. Native/CLI clients send no `Sec-Fetch-Site` header so they pass through regardless.

## Related

- Sibling enforcement: **#98924** (`allowedOriginPatterns`, open) — which origins are allowed.
- Prior art (closed security findings this complements): **#102834** (HTTP ingress CSRF under `auth.mode=none`), **#96486** (CSRF via the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback`, which this PR reuses verbatim rather than duplicating).
- Prior attempt by me: **#35109** (closed) — see "Prior Attempt & What Improved".

cc @steipete — this sits on the gateway origin/security boundary you own (and is the sibling of #98924 / the closed #102834, #96486). The `Sec-Fetch-Site` reject is scoped to the WS upgrade pre-handshake specifically because of the MCP-HTTP caveat you handled; happy to align flag names / gate position with #98924 before merge if you'd prefer.


---

## ClawSweeper Follow-up (head `1b5c1de`)

Addressed all four findings from the July 17 ClawSweeper review in a single follow-up commit (`1b5c1de7ed5`):

1. **[P1] Default-on Sec-Fetch-Site reject → opt-in.** `rejectCrossSiteWebSocketRequests` now defaults to `false` (`=== true` instead of `!== false`), matching this PR's stated "all flags default-off" design and preserving the v2026.4.15 / PR #66665 loopback-alias contract that browsers legitimately flag as `Sec-Fetch-Site: cross-site`. Regression test added (`allows legitimate loopback cross-site traffic by default`).
2. **[P1] Duplicate config field removed.** `gateway.security.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` is gone; `verify-client` now reads the existing `gateway.controlUi.dangerouslyAllowHostHeaderOriginFallback` so pre-handshake and post-handshake admission share one source of truth.
3. **[P2] Canonical IPv6 parsing.** `forwarded-headers.ts` now uses `normalizeIpAddress` from `@openclaw/net-policy/ip` instead of `split(":")[0]`. Bracketed / unbracketed / port-suffixed IPv6 literals all normalize correctly. Regression tests added for IPv6 contradiction detection and matching-across-forms.
4. **[P2] Public config contract completed.** `gateway.security` plus its three leaf fields now have entries in `schema.labels.ts`, `schema.tags.ts`, and `schema.help.ts` (all ≥80 chars with operational guidance, per `schema.help.quality.test.ts`).

Net diff: +50/-40 prod LOC across 8 files. The PR got smaller, not larger. All unit tests (`verify-client`: 8/8, `schema.help.quality`: 22/22) and `tsgo` core typecheck are green on the new head.
